# pai home

Where PAI keeps its files; move them out of ~/.claude

```
pai home <command>
```

Where PAI keeps its files; move them out of ~/.claude.

```sh
pai home path
pai home migrate --dry-run
```

### pai home path

Print where PAI's home is

```
pai home path
```

Print where PAI's home is.

The resolved PAI_HOME: $PAI_HOME, else ~/.pai, else ~/.claude/pai until `pai home migrate` has run.

```sh
pai home path
```

See also: `pai home migrate`

### pai home migrate

Move PAI's home from ~/.claude/pai to ~/.pai

```
pai home migrate [options]
```

Move PAI's home from ~/.claude/pai to ~/.pai.

Refuses while the daemon, router or any worker runs. Renames every entry of ~/.claude/pai into ~/.pai (stops on name clashes; ~/.pai/pgdata is never touched), moves leftovers (*.migrated-*, *.bak*, tarballs) to ~/.pai/attic/<date>/, leaves ~/.claude/pai as a symlink to ~/.pai, rewrites ~/.claude/pai paths in config.yaml, workers.yaml and PAI's launchd plists, and prints a before/after table. See docs/pai-home.md.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | flag | — | Print exactly what would happen, change nothing |

```sh
pai home migrate --dry-run
pai home migrate
```

See also: `pai home path`, `pai config migrate`

## Subcommands

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `pai home path` | Print where PAI's home is |
| `pai home migrate` | Move PAI's home from ~/.claude/pai to ~/.pai |
